newsitem.title: TURKEY: Pro-Baghdad Iraqi Kurds leave Turkey for U.S.
newsitem.headline: Pro-Baghdad Iraqi Kurds leave Turkey for U.S.

text.p: Senior members of a pro-Baghdad Iraqi Kurdish group losing ground in fighting in northern Iraq have left Turkey bound for talks with U.S. officials in Washington, Iraqi Kurdish officials said on Tuesday.
"They left last night," Faik Nerwiye of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) told Reuters. "They are on the way to Washington."

KDP leaders Sami Abdurrahman said on Monday he would bring up alleged Iranian support for the rival Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), whose forces have retaken whole swathes of northern Iraq one month after being expelled by the KDP.
The KDP last month gained control of most of northern Iraq from the PUK with the aid of the Iraqi military.
The group invited Iraqi forces into the Western-protected region which had been a virtual no-go area for Baghdad since 1991.

The United States responded to the Iraqi move by firing cruise missiles at military installations in southern Iraq, but was forced to abandon military, intelligence and aid operations in northern Iraq.
Iran on Monday denied KDP allegations that it was backing the PUK offensive with manpower, arms and ammunition.
